name: Barak Van Wyk Coaching: Closing Playbook (derived from calls)
source: There is no written script. Derived from 14 recorded closer calls in closer_all.json, of which 12 Zoom calls were read in full (all run by Makena Waterhouse, Sep to Nov 2026). The 2 Drive calls (recG83GHIMQ9gNUul, recuD9fhc8NSBGK9z) are still being transcribed and are not used as evidence either way. Of the 12 read, 2 are won (Call Outcome 'Closed' and Payment Type not 'Deposit' or 'Instalment Paid'): recGhnRsvZefXBVSx (individual, first month 1500) and recCs5H4hJqOJtQip (One Call Session 500). 4 more closed on a first instalment or deposit (rec6IqrIcBNPKz9e9, recbpZf1niLOSFMfR, reckX0EYFDCGQ5w0o, recJJyTCIcSpWhIZE) and are used as supporting evidence only. 6 did not close (5 Offer Made, 1 Lost) and are the contrast set. With only 2 strict wins this is a thin base; re-check once the Drive calls are in. Checks marked '(best practice: missing on his calls)' are standard high-ticket steps added only where the non-closing calls show their absence hurt.

sanctioned_offer.cadence: weekly 1-hour session with Barak (both partners), couples exercises and individual homework between sessions
sanctioned_offer.payment_plan: 3 x 1800 monthly (900 bi-weekly offered once). Not shown on the 2 strict wins; price and plan come from the instalment closes (recbpZf1niLOSFMfR, reckX0EYFDCGQ5w0o) and the offer-made calls. One close took half up front (2700).

sanctioned_offer.cadence: weekly 1-hour 1:1 session with Barak plus homework
sanctioned_offer.payment_plan: 3 x 1500 monthly. Both won Zoom calls quote 4500 total; one won call started on the 1500 first month. 1800 was never quoted for an individual. One deposit call quoted the first session at 300 and took a 100 deposit, which is off-sheet.
Paid in full. Credited toward the 12-week program if they continue.

offer_includes: 12 weekly 1-hour Zoom sessions with Barak (couples meet him together, sometimes separately), homework and couples exercises between sessions, a structured path: find why the cheating or lying happened, trace it to its emotional and developmental origins, repair the impulse, attachment and validation systems, and build new internal controls; for the hurt partner, healing from betrayal trauma, clarity and self-trust. End state: rebuild into a secure partnership, or separate with closure.
rules: No outcome promise. Promise the process and the answer: by week 12 they either rebuild or separate with closure. Say 'this isn't about staying together at all costs.'
Never excuse the cheating and never take sides. Name the partner's part without making it a justification.
Hear from each person first, before the closer's own read. In couples, ask both partners every key question.
The buyer must want change for themselves, not only to keep the partner. Check this out loud.

Present the 12-week program first at full price. Step down to a first month or one call only after the program is pitched and only when the hesitation is about certainty, not to dodge a money objection.
Every step-down is credited toward the full program and comes with Barak's booking link on the same call.
Take payment and book Barak while still on the call. 'Think about it' is not an ending; get a dated next step.
If the '80% of couples stay together' stat is used, frame it as a track record, never as what will happen for them.
Do not argue with a skeptical or sales-savvy prospect about the call itself. Restate the purpose of the call and the next step.
Recording disclosure: none of the 14 calls tells the prospect the call is recorded. Add a one-line disclosure at the open (compliance item, not a closing lever).

checks.text: Introduces self and role ('I help Barak with his client application process')
Confirms they still have about 45 minutes and a private, quiet spot (not driving, not at work)
References what Barak or the setter shared, then asks to hear it from them first
Confirms everyone who decides on the money is on the call, or gets agreement to decide without them
checks.conditional: only if a partner or money decision-maker exists

checks.text: Sets the agenda: understand the situation, see if Barak can help, and if so get the first session booked today (best practice: missing on his calls)
Asks what they want to achieve, for themselves or the relationship
In couples, asks each partner separately and reflects each answer back
checks.conditional: only if both partners are on

checks.text: Asks whether the goal is to stay together if there is a clear path to healing
Asks the partner who strayed whether they want this for themselves, not just for the other person
Gets how long ago it happened and how it came out (told, found out, trickle truth)
Asks whether it was once or a pattern, and how long the pattern goes back
Asks whether it has stopped or the hurt partner fears it is continuing
Asks the hurt partner how it felt to find out
Keeps detail to what matters and pauses a couple who start fighting on the call
checks.conditional: only if the couple argues on the call

checks.text: Asks what feeling they were after, or what void it filled
Asks where it comes from (childhood, past relationships, self-worth)
Challenges the easy answer ('if it were that simple you would have stopped')
Normalizes not knowing why: that is what the work with Barak is for
Asks permission to be honest, then names the mixed signals or justifications back to them
Asks whether the behavior fits who they want to be ('is that how you want to be known?')
Asks the strayer how it feels to hear the partner's hurt and whether they understand why trust is gone
checks.conditional: only if both partners are on

checks.text: Holds the line that the partner's faults or the marriage's problems do not justify cheating, without judging
States plainly that Barak can only help someone with a real will to change

phases.name: What they tried and why now

checks.text: Asks what they have tried (therapy, pastor, rehab, self-help, nothing)
Asks why it did not work or why they stopped
Asks why now, after living with it this long
Asks what in Barak's content made them think he is the right fit
Asks the ideal outcome at the end of 12 weeks
Asks who that will help them become
Asks how that would feel, for each partner where both are on
Asks what happens if nothing changes in 6 to 12 months
Asks whether that is something they are willing to settle for
Ties the cost to the people they care about (kids, partner, themselves)
Asks if they believe change is possible for them
Asks if they are ready to commit to the work, regardless of how the relationship turns out
Reassures: 'your situation is not inconsistent with the people we work with'
Asks what they were told about the investment and corrects any mismatch before the pitch (best practice: missing on his calls)
Frames it as not traditional talk therapy: action, accountability, homework, only 12 weeks
Walks the steps: find the why, trace it to its origins, repair impulse and validation systems, build new controls; healing for the hurt partner
Ties the steps to the words they used earlier (their kids, their self-trust, their partner)
Gives the end state: rebuild a secure partnership or separate with closure, not staying together at all costs
Explains delivery: weekly 1-hour sessions with Barak plus work between sessions
Makes no outcome promise ('not an overnight thing')
Checks for questions or understanding
States the full price for their program (5400 couples, 4500 individual) and that it can be broken up
Asks 'assuming we can figure out the financial side, is this something you want to move forward with?'
Separates belief from money: 'finances aside, do you feel this can actually help you?'
Offers the monthly plan (1800 or 1500) when they cannot pay in one go
Asks what is really holding them back and isolates it: have the money but unsure, have some, or a real stretch
Works the real block (fear, identity, trust in Barak) with questions before touching price
Points out that thinking it over will not answer it; meeting Barak will
Steps down to the first four sessions or one call, credited to the full program
checks.conditional: only if hesitation is about certainty

checks.text: Gets both partners' own yes before taking payment
checks.conditional: only if both partners are on

checks.text: If they still need time, books a dated reconnect on the call rather than 'text me' (best practice: missing on his calls)
checks.conditional: only if no payment on the call

phases.name: Take payment and book Barak live

checks.text: Sends the payment link by text or email while still on the call
Stays on until the payment goes through, solving card, bank or fraud-hold problems live
Sends Barak's onboarding and booking link and gets a session booked
Asks them to pick a time they can commit to, within the next week
Says she will brief Barak on what they shared and ends warm

segments.strayer_alone: The person who cheated or lied comes in alone wanting to know why and to stop the pattern; partner absent, sometimes skeptical or waiting to see change.
segments.couple_in_crisis: Both partners on the call after discovery or trickle truth; the hurt partner wants proof and the why, the strayer wants to keep the relationship. Often fights on the call.
segments.betrayed_partner_alone: The hurt partner comes alone, anxious or numb, unsure whether to stay; the other partner will not join. Sold on clarity, self-trust and peace either way.
segments.serial_or_compulsive: Long-running pattern (sex addiction, sex workers, dating apps, serial affairs), often with past therapy or rehab that did not hold; ambivalent about wanting a relationship at all.
segments.other: Does not fit. Propose a label in signals[0].
